summary: Guidance for staged rollback of mixed quantization + adaptive batching + KV prefetch in prod
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sharp increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xxs after enabling a combined optimization profile (q4 quantization + adaptive batching + KV prefetch) on their dedicated workloads. The tenant is NovaraHealth (enterprise) running pinned model variants in prod us-east.

Impact:
- Elevated 95th/99th latency impacting API SLAs for critical patient triage flows (spikes to 2.5s from baseline ~300ms).
- ~5% request error rate (502/524) reported over last 3h.
- Customer requests stepwise, low-risk rollback guidance that avoids broad capacity churn.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: novara-prod-pool (reserved GPUs)
- Model variants: rw-gpt-3b-q4_8 pinned, fallback: rw-gpt-3b-fp16
- Autoscaling policy: conservative (no aggressive scale-up)
- Observability: Console traces + per-route latency graphs available (link in comments).

Steps observed / how the change was applied:
1) On 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, customer applied an optimizer profile bundle that set: quant_profile=q4_8, adaptive_batching=enabled (max_batch=64, dynamic_threshold=120ms), kv_prefetch=aggressive
2) Within ~30–45 minutes, error rate climbs and tail latency regresses.
3) Customer toggled kv_prefetch off for a single route (canary) with partial improvement, but errors persisted across other routes.

Repro/Notes:
- Repro is intermittent; load shape correlates with bursty user arrivals causing large batches to form that time out on slower token-generation paths.
- KV prefetch appears to increase memory pressure on some GPUs when combined with quantized kernels, leading to OOM-like behavior surfaced as 5xx.
- Adaptive batching settings make rollback tricky: instant disable may drop throughput and cause queueing across tenants.

Customer asks:
- A clear, minimal-risk sequence to unwind optimizations that minimizes service disruption and avoids a full fleet restart.
- Confirmation of which knob to toggle first (kv_prefetch vs adaptive_batching vs quant_profile).
- Any temporary mitigations (timeouts, per-route limits) we can apply now.
comments: 2026-03-12 15:01 UTC - Liam Chen (Support): Thanks Aisha — we've triaged and reproduced a similar spike in the staging replay. Will propose a staged rollback sequence below and coordinate maintenance windows with NovaraHealth.
2026-03-12 16:10 UTC - Aisha Gomez (Support): Customer confirms they cannot tolerate >500ms P95 during business hours. They asked to avoid global restarts. Contact is Sara Mills (NovaraHealth SRE).

2026-03-12 17:05 UTC - Liam Chen (Support): Initial hypothesis: combined memory-pressure from kv_prefetch + q4 kernel memory layout causes transient GPU OOMs; adaptive batching amplifies queue depth making failures visible. Proposed first step: reduce kv_prefetch aggression for the tenant (prefetch_items=1) and monitor 30 minutes.

2026-03-13 01:22 UTC - Sara Mills (Customer): We applied kv_prefetch=1 to two high-traffic routes. Latency improved on those routes (~20% P95 drop) but errors persisted on background inference route. Need next steps.

2026-03-13 03:10 UTC - Liam Chen (Support): Next: transition adaptive_batching from 'aggressive' to 'conservative' for tenant (max_batch=16, dynamic_threshold=400ms) for remaining routes. This reduces batching pressure while preserving some throughput. We'll keep quant_profile intact as last resort.
investigation_notes: Staging replay with identical load shape reproduced 502s when kv_prefetch=aggressive + q4_8 present. GPU memory high-water marks hit ~95% at failure windows.
Heap and kernel logs show transient allocation failures in q4 kernel path; FP16 kernels did not show same behavior under identical load.
Per-route tracing indicates most 5xxs originate in decoder token generation stage (long sequences).
resolution_notes:
Staged unwind sequence agreed with customer (low risk):
  1) Reduce kv_prefetch intensity per-route to prefetch_items=1 (canary already applied) and observe 30–60m.
  2) If errors remain, set adaptive_batching to conservative (max_batch=16, dynamic_threshold=400ms) for affected tenant routes.
  3) If tail latency still unacceptable and errors persist, roll quant_profile back to fp16 for the largest-model route only (keep q4 on low-traffic routes).
  4) If rollback of quant_profile is required, do per-shard gradual switch to avoid immediate capacity pressure (1 shard per 10 minutes).

Applied: Step 1 and 2 completed by Novara SRE with Support assistance. Observed 72% reduction in 5xxs and P95 improved to ~420ms on critical routes.
Follow-ups: schedule a post-mortem with engineering to review q4 kernel memory behavior and add a guard that prevents kv_prefetch=aggressive from being enabled concurrently with q4_8 for dedicated tenants without explicit QA.
follow_up_actions: ENG: Create a short-term guard in the optimizer controller to block aggressive KV prefetch when q4_8 is active for dedicated pools (linked PR).
DX: Update docs for recommended rollback order and a troubleshooting checklist for optimizer bundles.
SRE: Run a capacity-replay test with mixed quant profiles and kv_prefetch settings to validate fix.
CS: Share post-mortem and recommended config templates with NovaraHealth by 2026-03-18.
